A genome attack on a single hash value can require an immense amount of computing power, especially if the hash is strong. The power of the rainbow table attack is that it pre-computes and stores the results of the hash function for a vast number of possible passwords.

This approach massively speeds up the process by turning a linear search (brute force) into an associative search. However, the catch is that rainbows tables are only useful when there is a *lot* of data in the database that the attacker is willing disclose. It's also a very bad and illegal way to conduct an internet black-box attack.
